peer_positioning.text: Aena has the highest EBITDA margin in the airport group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2025}}), against a peer median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Cash generation also leads the group, with FFO to debt and FCF to debt both ranking {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2025}} against peer medians of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}} respectively.
Leverage sits in the middle of the group, with net leverage ranking {{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}} and gross leverage ranking {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} and FCF to debt by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}, as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.
Margins: the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, a weaker result than the prior year even as revenue rose by {{revenue.change@FY2025}}.

Investment: capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}, but the increase in capital spending absorbs a larger share of cash generated.
Regulation: the regulator set the average airport charge for 2026 above the prior year's level, so the tariff path under the next regulatory period remains the key revenue sensitivity.
